summary: Iteration 4: tested Recruiter Talent search, profile links (verify page, dashboard/CTF/drill leaderboards, streak share card) and Streak Freeze (buy + auto-apply + archive) end-to-end, backend and UI. Backend: 10/10 new pytest pass. Frontend: one CRITICAL bug found and fixed. The Drill page crashed with 'ProfileLink is not defined' when the Leaderboard tab was opened, because Drill.jsx used ProfileLink without importing it. I added the import and retested: drill leaderboard links now show for public profiles and plain text for private ones. Everything else worked on first run.

minor.issue: streak_stats() calls apply_freeze() as a side effect, so anonymous recruiter browsing and other users viewing leaderboards spend other users' freezes. The outcome matches the 'auto-apply' design, but public GET endpoints change data, and talent runs about 10+ DB queries per candidate (N+1). That is fine at 8 users (0.2s) but will not scale to 300.

Freezes are only applied when the user's data is read. A user who missed yesterday and holds an unapplied freeze is therefore not in the 'alive' set, and gets no rescue email even though their streak is protected. Suggest calling apply_freeze for drill users (submission on today-2) before computing alive.

ui_bugs.issue: Runtime crash 'ProfileLink is not defined' (missing import) — FIXED by testing agent

issues: Rank, certificate and skill filters use native <select> elements with the browser's default dropdown, not the shadcn Select used elsewhere. Works, but looks inconsistent with the dark theme.
